advocate

/AD-vuh-kit/ (noun) · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Advocate is publically support something.

The lawyer became a strong advocate for children's rights.

Example

Every month, a retired nurse stands up at the town meeting to argue for a free health clinic. She writes letters to the newspaper, collects signatures outside the grocery store, and never misses a chance to speak in public as the clinic's most devoted advocate.

She doesn't just privately agree the clinic is a good idea — she publicly speaks and campaigns on its behalf, which is what makes her an advocate. Advocate is more precise than 'supporter' because it names someone who actively and openly argues for a cause, not someone who merely favors it.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

proponent: A proponent argues in favor of a particular idea, plan, or proposal -- the proponent of a new tax. An advocate speaks up for a cause, group, or person, often on someone else's behalf, and keeps making the case in public. You propose ideas as a proponent; you stand up for people as an advocate.

champion: A champion is a devoted public defender of a cause, with a heroic, whole-hearted ring -- the champion of the underdog. An advocate is the plainer, everyday word for someone who publicly argues and campaigns for a cause. Champion adds glory and total devotion to what an advocate already does.

campaigner: A campaigner pushes a cause through organized activity -- rallies, drives, door-to-door work. An advocate may do all of that, but the heart of being an advocate is speaking on a cause's or person's behalf. A campaigner organizes the push; an advocate gives the cause its voice.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

opponent: a person who argues against something

detractor: someone who belittles or criticizes something

Where it sits · how actively you back the cause

sympathizer → supporter → advocate → crusader

sympathizer vs. advocate: A sympathizer is weaker than an advocate — a sympathizer privately agrees with a cause, while an advocate speaks up for it in public.

supporter vs. advocate: A supporter is slightly weaker than an advocate; a supporter backs a cause, but an advocate actively argues and campaigns for it.

crusader vs. advocate: A crusader is stronger than an advocate — an advocate makes the public case for a cause, while a crusader devotes nearly everything to fighting for it.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — ad-: to, toward (Latin)

root — voc: to call; voice (Latin (vocare))

suffix — -ate: forming a noun: one who is (called) (Latin)

Put it together: Ad- (toward) + voc (call) + -ate: an advocate is literally 'one called to' another's side to speak for them — a person who publicly voices support for a cause.

Use the root in a new word: vocabulary: Her grandfather did not find his true vocation until he was nearly forty.

Root Check

Word Choice

Advocate is taught here as the noun — a specific person who speaks up for a cause, group, or person (a patient advocate, an advocate for reform) — not the related verb 'to advocate for something,' which names the act itself rather than the person doing it.
